items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: There was a fellow -- youngster -- young boy from Charleston, South Carolina, by the name of Russell Brown

ctx.x: This is back in the '20's, right?

Yes, that was in '21, I think. There were many things that happened at Leroy's but I do remember something that had an impact on the whole world. There was a fellow -- youngster -- young boy from Charleston, South Carolina, by the name of Russell Brown, and he didn't have any work but he could do the dance that they did in Charleston, South Carolina, called the cut out. And we put him on for him to do his dance every night and then people would throw money on the floor to him and that's how the youngster made a…

York and trying to make it, and every night he'd come in and get his ration -- he'd go around to all the cabarets, so he was nicknamed Charleston, because he came from Charleston and everybody called him that. "Charleston, want to do your dance?" and they'd put him on. And he'd do this cut out. So eventually they'd say, "Do the Charleston, Charleston, do the Charleston." And the name of the dance originated in New York City because in Charleston itself it was called the cut out. But it became Charleston in New…
